did_you_know.text: Did you know? Josiah did not act alone: he summoned the elders of Judah and Jerusalem, thereby involving the nation’s leaders in the religious reform.
Did you know? After reading the Book of the Covenant, Josiah made a covenant before the LORD, and all the people pledged themselves to uphold it.

Did you know? The cleansing of the Temple included removing the objects used in the worship of Baal, Asherah, and the whole host of heaven, burning them outside Jerusalem, and carrying their ashes to Bethel.
Did you know? Josiah defiled and destroyed the high places throughout Judah, from Geba to Beersheba, seeking to put an end to the worship carried out there.
Did you know? The king defiled Topheth in the Valley of Ben-Hinnom to prevent the sacrifice of children by fire to Molech.
Did you know? Josiah destroyed the altar at Bethel, which had been built in the days of Jeroboam son of Nebat and is described in the chapter as the altar that led Israel into sin.
Did you know? When Josiah discovered the tomb of the man of God, he ordered that his bones not be disturbed; in this way, the bones of the prophet who had come from Samaria were also preserved.
Did you know? Josiah’s Passover is described as an event unlike any celebrated since the days of the judges, or during the reigns of any of the kings of Israel or Judah who preceded him.

Did you know? Despite Josiah’s faithfulness to the LORD, the chapter emphasizes that the LORD’s great anger against Judah did not subside, because of the sins of Manasseh and the offenses with which he had angered the LORD.
Did you know? Josiah was killed at Megiddo when he went out to confront Pharaoh Neco, king of Egypt, and after his death he was brought to Jerusalem for burial.
